topics.caution: The doctor's sarcastic bluff to નરરત્ન — 'જેટલી તારા નામની માળા જપી છે એટલી પ્રભુના નામની ફેરવી હોત તો absolutely painless processથી મુક્તિ મળી હોત' — could be flattened into a claim that chanting God's name is more effective than medicine, or dwelt on as a statement about a patient's death.
topics.guidance: In `explanation`, frame the line as revealing the doctor's careless bravado and poor bedside manner toward an imagined patient he never actually treated (part of the second ચોટ building toward his exposure) — not as commentary on faith curing illness, and without dwelling on or restating the death implication.

topics.caution: The stage direction 'તમાચો મારે છે' (the doctor slaps નરરત્ન) could be presented as a satisfying comic payoff a child might imitate; separately, નરરત્નનું 'છતી આંખે છોકરીને કૂવામાં નાખી' (a printed idiom meaning 'put in distress', per the chapter's own કૂવામાં નાખવું gloss) could be stretched into commentary on arranged marriage or on the daughter, none of which the text states.
topics.guidance: In `explanation` and any `real_life_example`, present the slap as the exposed fraud's own petty, foolish reaction at being caught out — never as justice, and never something to act out — and read નરરત્નની 'કૂવામાં નાખી' line strictly as a father's regret at being deceived by the son-in-law's false claims (per the idiom's own printed meaning), without adding any view on marriage customs or on the daughter that the chapter itself does not state.
